summary_proposal.value: Two sources add comparisons of fragmentomic feature sets on shared plasma samples. Both are retrospective case-control analyses with internal or small external validation, and neither shows screening performance or clinical benefit. Hou et al. 2024 re-implemented ten published fragmentation patterns and DELFI with one support vector machine each on the DELFI 2019 cohort (208 cancers, 215 healthy). In 10 x 10-fold cross-validation the pan-cancer AUC ranged from 0.8741 (fragment length) to 0.9736 (5' end motif) within open chromatin regions; their DELFI re-implementation reached 0.9575. Their supplementary tables add sensitivity at 95% and 85% specificity and three independent cohorts, where rankings changed: on 46 lung cancers and 385 healthy individuals the end-motif model fell to AUC 0.5355 and sensitivity 0.0652 at 95% specificity, while fragment size distribution reached 0.9386 and 0.7174. Two tables in that supplementary file disagree on the sensitivity of the same models (evidence concern), so its values should not be cited until resolved. Wang et al. 2026, the UNITE developers (values rounded here to three decimals), stratified cancers by ichorCNA tumour fraction in pooled public and new 0.1x data. For cancers with tumour fraction of 3% or less, cross-validated AUC was 0.878 for all features combined, 0.873 for fragment length, 0.857 for SD of length counts, 0.736 for copy number, 0.715 for C/T end-motif ratio and 0.651 for short/long ratio, against 0.603 for a classifier using the ichorCNA tumour fraction alone, which detected 0.058 of these cancers at 95% specificity. For cancers with tumour fraction above 3% and up to 10%, the ichorCNA classifier reached 0.983, above the combined model (0.962) and copy number alone (0.926). The extracted UNITE tables give sensitivity at a fixed specificity only for the ichorCNA comparator; no source gives fragmentomic sensitivity at 98% or 99% specificity within a low tumour-fraction stratum.
